title: 40 cm soft-stall rotor with 170-180 Kv feed and 0.80 N-m spring-disc plus dump shutdown
problem_restatement: Build a 40 cm wind turbine that fits in a 45 cm cube, makes regulated power from 5 to 11 m/s, survives 22 m/s, and shuts down below 10% speed within 10 s on command or load loss and stays parked.
mechanism_sentence: Wind spins a 40 cm three-blade rotor to make electricity for a steady load, and if the stop button is pressed or the load is lost a spring squeezes a disc while extra spin turns to heat to stop in under 1 s and stay stopped.
decisive_choices: Choose SD7080 TSR 6 Cp 0.34 rotor (C2) over generic 3-blade (C1) because C2 gives quantified low-wind power 3.27 W at 5 m/s (E11) and 34.7 W at 11 m/s (E12) from available powers (E9)(E10) per source (E3) with same 40 cm fit as winner practice (E2).

Keep direct-drive outrunner plus bridge (C14) but correct winding to 170 to 180 Kv because 220 Kv low volts 6.50 V (E37) sits below 8 V regulator minimum (E60) per O2, while 170 Kv gives 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top (E76) inside 8 to 40 V with unchanged rotor speeds and shaft powers.

Choose upsized 0.80 N-m spring-applied solenoid-released disc plus 4 ohm dump (C21 as upsized) over dump alone (C16) which fails at 9123 rpm with 0.155 N-m vs 0.48 N-m aero (E48) because only combined brake crosses 315 rpm in 0.673 s and holds at 0 rpm at 10 s with margins 1.67 and 1.11 (E70) satisfying 10 s rule (E41).
open_question: Do bench tests confirm power curve, timed stop, re-latch restart and parked torque on built hardware?
transfer_line: Energy: three-blade rotor -> outrunner generator -> dump resistor grid | Measured: overspeed switch -> latching relay

assumed_constraints.constraint: Rotor Cp 0.34 at TSR 6 for SD7080 low-Reynolds sections
assumed_constraints.source: Design of Small Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine for Low Wind Speed Rural Applications

assumed_constraints.constraint: 6061-T6 aluminum yield about 276 MPa for post and nacelle
Buck-boost regulator needs 8 V minimum and accepts 8 to 40 V to make regulated 12 V

concept.working_principle: A 40 cm SD7080 fixed-pitch rotor with soft stall on a stiff nacelle-post mount drives a 170-180 Kv direct-drive outrunner through a Schottky bridge to a buck-boost feed to tunnel load plus switched 4 ohm dump grid, with a series normally-closed e-stop plus load-volt tap plus centrifugal overspeed switch latching trip driving a 0.80 N-m spring-applied disc plus dump brake on the low-speed shaft with wiring inside nacelle and post bore.

parts.name: Direct-drive outrunner generator
parts.material: copper and steel outrunner 170 to 180 Kv

parts.name: Buck-boost regulator
parts.material: electronics buck-boost 8 to 40 V to 12 V

parts.name: Normally closed safety chain loop
parts.material: copper wiring with relay and switches

constraint_table.how_shown: Side clearance and axial stack were summed and checked against deflection inside the cube layout.
Shaft powers from available wind were carried through bridge and regulator to regulated load at revised volts.
Survival thrust and moment were carried to post stress and checked against aluminum yield.

constraint_table.constraint: Shut down to below 10% of top speed within 10 s on command and on disconnect and stay there
constraint_table.design_value: 0.673 s to 315 rpm, 0 rpm at 10 s
constraint_table.how_shown: Combined dump plus 0.80 N-m disc simulation was checked to cross threshold and hold at zero.

measurement_chain.name: centrifugal overspeed switch with load voltage tap and stop button
measurement_chain.interface: normally closed loop opens on overspeed or load loss or button press

measurement_chain.name: latching safety relay
measurement_chain.interface: latched trip signal that stays tripped without power

measurement_chain.name: brake relay and buck-boost controller
measurement_chain.interface: switched power between tunnel load and dump grid

fabrication_steps.description: Assemble steel post clamp and aluminum post first, because nacelle bedplate and wiring mount to it and set cube position
Build stiff nacelle bedplate with two-bearing housing and brake rails next, because shaft, generator and caliper reaction feed into it
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted 6061 aluminum plate bedplate, 250 mm long

fabrication_steps.description: Make 40 cm three-blade SD7080 rotor on rigid hub with spinner and fit with tilt and overhang, because clearance depends on assembled deflection
Wire outrunner plus Schottky bridge to buck-boost and 4 ohm dump grid and normally-closed chain to spring disc last, because electrics thread inside nacelle and post bore clear of disc
fabrication_steps.method: Wired outrunner 170 to 180 Kv with 4 ohm dump resistor

risks.risk: Dump-only brake gives zero torque at zero speed and runs away at 22 m/s
risks.mitigation: Use combined 0.80 N-m spring disc plus 4 ohm dump with soft-stall blades keeping parked torque near 0.25 N-m below hold

risks.risk: 220 Kv low-wind volts 6.50 V starve regulator and false-trip load sense
risks.mitigation: Rewind to 170-180 Kv giving 8.41 V low to 18.5 V top inside 8-40 V regulator window

novelty_claim: Locomotive rheostatic dump-grid feed plus elevator safety-chain normally-closed latching sense transferred to model scale with spring-applied disc plus soft-stall rotor for fail-safe stop and park.

figure_spec.system_view: Side-elevation shutdown with left-to-right wind driving rotor plus hub plus shaft to generator plus spring disc brake in nacelle to controller and load, post below cube

open_questions: Do bench tests confirm power curve, timed stop, re-latch restart and parked torque on built hardware?
